problem: Existing EmbodiedQA systems (PACMAN, NMC) use hierarchical navigation modules trained with RL and still navigate poorly in unseen environments, especially at medium and long distances. Question-only blind baselines match QA accuracy, so QA accuracy alone is an insufficient metric.
motivation: The paper argues that navigation, measured by the change in distance to the target, should be evaluated alongside QA accuracy, since QA is bottlenecked by an agent's failure to reach the target in new scenes. The authors therefore build a simple end-to-end baseline and relax the setting so the agent can adapt to a new environment.
key_idea: Train a plain LSTM navigation policy by imitating shortest paths and jointly with the QA module by SGD (no RL), then adapt it to each new environment via a calibration stage that asks questions about randomly placed marker objects, using policy distillation to keep prior knowledge.
insight: A simple imitation-learned LSTM policy beats the more complex RL-trained hierarchical policies on navigation, so RL and hierarchy are not necessary. Calibration helps mainly at T-30 and T-50 (T-50 dD 2.36 to 3.39) and not at T-10, where the target is already visible. Distillation beats plain fine-tuning (3.39 vs 3.27 at T-50), and the lambda ablation peaks at 0.2, so balancing the marker policy loss against the distillation loss matters. More markers improve navigation.
method: Navigation module: 2-layer LSTM (cell size 128) takes observation, question embedding and previous action, and outputs the next action; trained by cross-entropy imitation of the shortest path with teacher forcing.
QA module: reuses the EQA v1 QA model, a 2-layer LSTM question encoder with dot-product attention over image features from the last 5 frames of the trajectory.

Joint SGD training without RL: the navigation module is initialized by imitation; the QA module is trained on ground-truth path observations, and predicted navigation trajectories are gradually incorporated (incremental learning) to close the train/test gap.

Calibration setting: at test time, 5 held-out SUNCG marker objects (mailbox, safe, shoes, tripod, cloth) are randomly placed in each environment, with the auto-generated question 'what is the color of the <marker>?' and A* shortest paths; 290 questions over 58 test environments.

Distillation adaptation: the adapted navigation LSTM is trained on marker paths with loss L = λ·L_d + (1-λ)·L_a, where L_a is the action cross-entropy and L_d = Σ(1 - cos(h^c, h^p)) against a frozen pre-trained model's hidden states; λ=0.2.
Evaluation: spawn the agent 10/30/50 actions from the target (T-10/T-30/T-50) and report dD (change in distance to target) plus QA accuracy.

setting.backbone: 2-layer LSTM navigation policy (cell 128) + 2-layer LSTM QA module with attention; pre-trained CNN from PACMAN as image encoder (trained from scratch on top)
setting.training_data: EQA v1 training split (648 environments, 7,190 questions) with shortest-path supervision; in the calibration setting, an additional 290 marker questions/paths in the 58 test environments
setting.observation: egocentric RGB only (first-person view, no map or GPS)
setting.action_space: low-level discrete: forward 0.5 m, turn left/right 9°, stop
setting.privileged: none in the standard setting; the calibration setting uses A* shortest paths to placed markers in test environments and known marker placement (adaptation before testing)

numbers.backbone: LSTM navigation + LSTM QA, SGD joint training
numbers.extra: no RL; dD reported at T-10/T-30/T-50 spawn distances

numbers.backbone: LSTM navigation + LSTM QA, adapted with policy distillation
numbers.extra: calibration setting: 5 markers/environment, 290 marker questions, A* shortest paths for adaptation

numbers.backbone: LSTM navigation + LSTM QA, fine-tuned on markers

numbers_note: Marker-count and lambda ablations are given only as figures (no numbers). EQA v1 is not among the canonical benchmark names, so it is labelled other:EQA-v1.
results: In the standard setting the simple baseline gets the best navigation dD (0.23/1.48/2.36) against PACMAN+REINFORCE (0.10/0.65/1.51) and NMC+A3C (0.09/1.15/1.70), and higher QA accuracy at T-30 and T-50 (48.01%/47.29% vs NMC+A3C 46.21%/44.32%). NMC+A3C is slightly better at T-10 QA (53.58% vs 52.91%). Calibration with distillation raises T-50 dD to 3.39 and QA to 48.83%.
limitations: The calibration setting needs extra test-environment interaction with markers and A* or hand-marked shortest paths, which weakens the comparison to the standard setting.
Absolute performance remains low (QA about 48% at T-30 and T-50), and calibration gives no gain at short distance (T-10).
Evaluation is on EQA v1 in House3D only, with baseline numbers copied from other papers; the marker set is small (5 objects).
